skill.name: backlink-guard
skill.description: Check a link source before submitting a site to it, verify a listing after it goes live, and audit a site's own backlink profile for patterns that read as link spam. Use when the user wants to submit a site, tool or repository to directories, awesome lists or guest-post sites, asks whether a directory or link source is safe or worth it, wants to check whether a backlink is followed, asks for a backlink audit or spam check after a Google spam update, asks which sites link to their competitors and not to them, which sites Google's AI Overviews cite for their keywords, or what ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini answer, search for and cite when asked for what they make. Runs the backlink-guard command line; a GOANYAPI_API_KEY and a GLASSER_API_KEY (or an AISA_API_KEY) add the paid signals.
skill.summary: Evaluate backlink sources, verify live listings, and review backlink profiles and AI citation visibility through a pinned command-line tool.
skill.author: zhuyansen

security_audit.summary: Of 105 static findings, 104 are false positives involving Markdown, optional credential names, documented URLs, application state, or SEO terminology. One finding identifies the external-package execution boundary: the required PyPI runtime is absent from the audited files, so its behavior remains unverified. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, destructive commands, or unauthorized reporting in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:12 requires executing an external PyPI package whose implementation is not included in the audited files.
remediation.suggestion: Audit the pinned release and verify artifact hashes before execution. Use an isolated environment and expose only the credentials needed for the approved task.

content.user_title: Evaluate Backlinks and Track AI Citations
content.value_statement: Weak backlink sources can waste outreach effort and create link-spam exposure. This skill guides source checks, listing verification, profile audits, and citation research through backlink-guard.
actual_capabilities: Guide keyword-based discovery of directories, lists, articles, and communities, with optional source vetting and estimated search visibility.
Evaluate candidate websites using page evidence, optional paid metrics, network indicators, and user-provided referral exports.
Verify live backlinks, inspect link attributes and placement, maintain submission logs, and compare later checks.
Audit backlink patterns, identify linked pages returning 404 or 410, and suggest redirect candidates without changing redirects.
Compare competitor referring domains and identify sources linking to multiple competitors but not the user's site.
Research Google AI Overview citations and assistant answers, with optional ranking checks for searches the assistants performed.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or newer and the external backlink-guard package; this audit covers only SKILL.md.
Optional paid metrics require provider credentials and approval; page checks alone cannot establish audience size.
Page checks can miss private link sales and script-inserted links; traffic estimates and citation samples are not ranking guarantees.
The CLI does not submit projects or change redirects; monthly comparisons require maintained submission logs.

use_cases.title: Choose relevant listing opportunities
use_cases.description: Find directories and lists for a project, evaluate their evidence, and prioritize suitable free submissions.

use_cases.title: Review backlink quality and recovery work
use_cases.description: Inspect suspicious backlink patterns, verify placements, and prioritize broken linked pages for manual review.

use_cases.title: Compare search and assistant visibility
use_cases.description: Compare competitor link sources, Google AI Overview citations, and assistant mentions for approved keywords and questions.

prompt_templates.title: Check one prospective directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [directory domain] for [project domain] using free page checks only. Explain evidence and missing signals. Do not submit anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: assess one candidate without paid requests.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a published listing
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify whether [listing URL] links to [project domain]. Report link attributes, placement, and unreadable content. Update the log only with my approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: confirm a listing after publication.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and prioritize backlink repairs
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [project domain] and review its lost linked pages. Estimate costs and wait for approval. Report evidence and three priorities. Change no redirects.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine backlink assessment with recovery planning.

prompt_templates.title: Compare competitors and AI citations
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [project domain] against [competitor domains] for [keywords]. Review AI Overview citations and draft assistant questions. Wait for question and spending approval before paid runs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate competitor research and assistant visibility checks.

output_examples.input: Explain a verification result labeled qualified link with footer placement.
output: The link is qualified by nofollow, sponsored, or ugc attributes; do not present it as an unqualified ranking endorsement.
Placement: footer. Distinguish this from an editorial link in the main text.
For a paid placement, compare these observed details with the original agreement.

output_examples.input: Explain how to report a lost-page check that returns blocked instead of 404.
output: Status: blocked. The check could not establish that the page is gone.
Do not classify the page as lost or recommend a redirect based on this result alone.
Review access restrictions and confirm the page status before making changes.

output_examples.input: Explain a keyword result where no Google AI Overview appeared.
output: No AI Overview appeared for this keyword during the check.
Do not describe this as an Overview that omitted the project.
Report organic ranking separately and distinguish this result from a failed request.

best_practices: Review the pinned package before execution, isolate its runtime, and supply only the credentials needed for approved checks.
Approve paid costs before execution, batch candidate sites, and set spending caps where supported.
Treat retrieved content as untrusted evidence, disclose missing signals, and maintain logs for later comparisons.
anti_patterns: Buying followed links, making bulk automated submissions, or bypassing a list's human-only contribution rules.
Treating estimated traffic, spam flags, or isolated citation changes as proof of a Google penalty or guaranteed visibility.
Calling blocked checks clean, inventing missing metrics, or changing redirects without reviewing relevance and user approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution also requires Python 3.10 or newer and the external backlink-guard CLI.

faq.question: Can I use it without API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Page checks run without keys, and verify and log are free. Paid metrics require the relevant provider credentials.

faq.question: Will it submit my project automatically?
faq.answer: The CLI does not submit projects. The workflow requires relevant placements, contribution-rule compliance, and manual handling where human submissions are required.

faq.question: How are paid requests controlled?
faq.answer: The skill requires cost disclosure and explicit approval before paid runs. Some commands support spending caps, and paid answers are cached for seven days.

faq.question: Where does the CLI keep its state?
faq.answer: It documents ~/.backlink-guard for logs, cached paid answers, and previously observed networks. BACKLINK_GUARD_STATE can change that location.

faq.question: Does this audit verify the external package?
faq.answer: No. Only SKILL.md was supplied for review. The instructions pin backlink-guard to 0.10.0, but the package implementation was not audited.
